answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent identity must lock a refundable bond before it can transact, and its reputation accrues slowly from verified work, like an opal forming layer by layer. Creating a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand bonds, while one misdeed slashes the bond and burns the reputation. Attackers face a mesa of cost: the tide of cheap identities cannot wash over a market where every identity carries real, losable stake.
